stem: A plant has yellowing and reduced vigor, and the stems carry colonies of aphids, shed skins and sticky honeydew. Which evidence is most directly useful for the pest diagnosis?
choices: Yellowing alone because crop symptoms identify aphid species.
The fertilizer record because aphids cannot cause yellowing.
Only the honeydew because no other sap-feeder can produce it.
The observed aphids plus cast skins and honeydew, interpreted with plant location and distribution.
rationale: Direct aphid observations supported by cast skins and honeydew provide stronger pest evidence than nonspecific crop symptoms or honeydew considered alone.
